deep.reconstruction: This page belongs to a section titled 'Inégalités de convexité et classes remarquables d'opérateurs'. The section is a preparation for singular-value inequalities used to study Schatten/von Neumann-type operator classes. The previous page states a 'fundamental lemma (H. Weyl)'. Let α_1≥…≥α_n and β be real sequences with partial sums α_1+…+α_m ≤ β_1+…+β_m for all m. Let φ be convex and symmetric on R^n, and assume either (a) φ is increasing in each variable, or (b) Σα_i = Σβ_i. Then φ(α) ≤ φ(β). The multiplicative corollary sets α_i = log ρ_i and β_i = log σ_i. It states: if f(e^{t_1},…,e^{t_n}) is convex and symmetric, ρ is decreasing, and ρ_1…ρ_m ≤ σ_1…σ_m for all m, then f(ρ) ≤ f(σ). The upper, crossed-out block of this page is a discarded attempt to settle the degenerate case where some ρ_i or σ_i vanish (only case (a) is affected, since (b) assumes the product is nonzero). The idea is to approximate (ρ,σ) by 'admissible' systems with positive entries and pass to the limit. Two devices appear: replacing σ_i by σ_i+ε, and reducing to the case σ_{n-1}>0, σ_n=0. There is also a trial normalisation ρ'_1…ρ'_n = σ'_1…σ'_n, and a side condition ρ'_i−ρ'_j ≤ σ'_i−σ'_j. The block ends with the simple choice ρ'_i = ρ_i, σ'_i = σ_i+ε, which keeps the product inequalities and makes σ' positive; positivity of ρ still has to be arranged, presumably by raising the zero ρ_i as the previous page says. The second part begins the proof of the lemma. A continuous convex φ on R^n is the supremum of affine functions L_k ≤ φ, because its epigraph is closed and convex and hence an intersection of closed half-spaces. If φ is increasing, every affine minorant L(t) = Σa_i t_i + b has all a_i ≥ 0. Indeed, if a_i < 0, letting t_i → −∞ sends L → +∞ while φ stays bounded above, contradicting L ≤ φ; the argument finishes on the next page. Using symmetry, the next page writes φ = sup_k sup_{σ∈S_n} σL_k. This reduces the lemma to sup_σ Σa_{σi}α_i ≤ sup_σ Σa_{σi}β_i, which follows from rearrangement plus Abel summation using the partial-sum hypothesis. This is a standard Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya / Karamata / Tomić–Weyl argument.
errors: Attribution: the additive majorization lemma is due to Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya (1929) and Karamata (1932), and the weak-majorization version (case a) to Tomić (1949) and Weyl (1949). Calling it 'Lemme fondamental (H. Weyl)' is only partly accurate, though Weyl did prove the multiplicative corollary for eigenvalues and singular values.

The crossed-out approximation argument is confused: it makes several restarts, has a stray mismatch between σ_i = σ'_i+ε and σ'_i = σ_i+ε, and tries an unnecessary product normalisation. The final choice σ'_i = σ_i+ε alone handles σ but not zero ρ_i, which must be treated separately as on the previous page. No mathematical error survives in the uncrossed text.
As stated on this page, 'φ continuous' is needed for the sup-of-affine representation; this is fine for finite convex functions on R^n.

It is preparatory material for singular-value inequalities, which Grothendieck later presented in his 1955 Bourbaki exposé on rearrangements and convexity inequalities in von Neumann algebras. Nothing here is new.
